LYSSIN    (Hydrophobinum*).
The  saliva  of  a  mad  dog.  A  nosode.

For  historical  review,  see  Bering's  Monograph  (Jv'orth  American  Journal  of
Homoeopathy,  1879).

The  first  saliva  was  obtained  by  Hering  in  August,  1833  (see  North  American
Journal  of  Homoeopathy,  1879),  and  proved  by  himself  in  the  same  year;  by
Schmid,  an  AUentown  student,  in  1835;  by  Behlert  on  a  number  of  pro  vers,  from
1835  to  1838;  by  Kedman  Coxe  on  himself  and  family,  in  1853;  by  Knerr,  with
the  300th  and  600th  of  Jenichen,  on  a  woman  bitten  by  a  dog,  not  rabid  in  1869.

Symptoms  observed  after  bites,  and  those  of  persons  afflicted  with  rabies,
collected  from  reliable  sources,  are  followed  by  a  dash  ( — ).

Clinical  reports  have  as  yet  been  meagre,  owing  to  the  comparatively  recent
publication  of  the  provings.
